cases.prompt: Find out what happens when the background workspace process disconnects after it starts returning a response. Explain why partial stdout or stderr cannot leak, exactly when the command runs locally instead, and how cancellation, completed command failures, and unexpected exceptions differ from recoverable infrastructure failures. Trace the source and focused tests. Don't just summarize docs or change files.
manualReviewCriteria: Traces DaemonClient and DaemonFallbackWorkspaceCommandRouter in src/RoslynKit, plus DaemonFallbackProcessIntegrationTests.
States that a disconnect after response start leaks neither partial stdout nor partial stderr because completed process results stay buffered.

States that only DaemonClientInfrastructureException emits one warning and performs exactly one standalone retry; cancellation, ordinary semantic failures, and unexpected failures do not use that recovery path.
Cites focused fallback and process-integration tests, not only daemon documentation.

cases.prompt: Find out how the repo keeps code-navigation requests on a consistent compiler view when tracked files change while reads are still running. Explain the maximum clean-reader capacity, pending-reload priority, what waits, when the old view is discarded, the exact quiet-period retry timing, and what happens if files change again during the retry load. Show the source and focused tests. Don't change files.
manualReviewCriteria: Traces src/RoslynKit/WorkspaceDaemonSession.cs and tests/RoslynKit.Tests/WorkspaceDaemonSessionTests.cs, including fingerprint and generation collaboration.
Explains the maximum of three clean readers, pending reload priority, reader draining, and when the old generation is discarded.
Explains the one 250 millisecond quiet-period retry; a second mismatch is served once from the new generation and marked nonreusable instead of exposing a mixed view.
Cites WorkspaceDaemonSessionTests or equivalent focused coverage.

cases.prompt: Why can an English-oriented code search return older results instead of waiting for an index update? Contrast an absent or unusable partition with a coherent stale partition, then trace nonblocking writer acquisition, state recapture, fresh-versus-stale fingerprint reporting, and transaction visibility so it is clear whether partial updates can become visible. Show the implementation and focused tests. Don't change files.
manualReviewCriteria: Traces SearchCommandService, SearchIndexFingerprint, and SqliteSearchIndex in src/RoslynKit, plus SearchCommandTests.
Explains that an absent or unusable partition waits, while a coherent existing partition uses a nonblocking writer lease and can answer stale during refresh.
Explains state recapture, atomic partition visibility, and fresh versus stale fingerprint reporting so partial updates never become visible.
Cites search command or SQLite index tests that cover stale, refresh, or replacement behavior.

cases.prompt: Starting only from this intent, find the RoslynKit code that extracts ordinary C# comments associated with a C# declaration and classifies each comment as leading, body, or trailing. Use actual repository search and navigation; do not assume declaration names or source files in advance. Trace the evidence path from ranked search results through a navigable symbol identity into bounded symbol context, then follow relevant connected syntax nodes or helpers to definitive source evidence. Explain search-result identity and excerpt provenance, trivia collection, supported comment kinds, nested-declaration ownership, normalization, location de-duplication, placement classification, descendant bounds, truncation, and focused test coverage. Cite precise production source and tests. Do not change files or Git state, build, restore, run tests, optimize code, or propose implementation changes. Do not merely summarize documentation.
manualReviewCriteria: Starts with intent-oriented search results and traces their opaque symbol identity and excerpt provenance into symbol-context.
Traces comment collection, supported line and block trivia, nearest-declaration ownership, normalization, and location de-duplication.
Explains the exact leading, trailing, and body placement rules using definitive source evidence.
Explains bounded descendants and truncation and follows a related helper or syntax node to focused evidence.
Cites production source and focused tests covering navigable search identities, comment metadata, placement, and truncation.
